card.title: Half a Beat Late
card.instruction: Use the group’s reactions as your cue, joining each one a moment late and escalating your enthusiasm to stay included.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely hilarious news about the mirror. Ha! Ha!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We weren't laughing. It's trapped the headmaster.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. That's my shocked laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes! Help! I'm extremely ahead on wanting that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You all laughed at the headmaster's face in that mirror? Ha! HA! Best staff party ever!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've stopped. He's trapped inside. Everyone's calling for help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help! HELP! I'll call the fire brigade and the mirror shop!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The caretaker's opening the back. We're thanking her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you! THANK YOU! I'll nominate you for caretaker of the year!

mechanism: A belatedly joins laughter, calls for help and thanks, amplifying each reaction to remain part of the group.
confusable: Unlike generic overenthusiasm, the successive group cues must be supplied by others and visibly change A's response.
comparison: This recovered alternative shifts from amusement to rescue to gratitude at a staff party; the sports alternative shifts between cheering and concern.
